There’s also a new trailer, showing some of the gunpowder-jumping and fishy boss-battling Hornet will get up to while exploring those sorrowful seas. Read more

title: Keep the lighthouse on and the villagers obedient in Glagstone, an eerie island city-builder with Macintosh-style graphics
description: Glagstone's "1-bit" aesthetic is a homage to Macintosh games of the late 1980s, cut with elements of art deco, Expressionism and film noir, but it looks like that mainly because it began life on lo-fi indie handheld Playdate. In transplanting this eerie, story-driven city-builder to Steam, developers Valerii Krasnoselskii and Evgenii Kirichenko have fleshed out the tasty throwback art and shored up connections between the game's management and story layers, while leaving the crux of the experience untouched: you are the newly appointed governor of a remote northern island, contested by rival nations. You have come here to harvest the island's rich mineral resources, and now, the island is trying to drive you nuts. Read more

title: Hollow Knight: Silksong’s First Major Expansion Arrives December 11, And It’s Free
description: Hollow Knight: Silksong developer Team Cherry has shown a first look at the upcoming Sea of Sorrow expansion. The first major--and free--expansion for Silksong takes players to a new aquatic region, with new areas to explore and new tools to master. You won't have to wait too long to play it either, as it's out on December 11. Team Cherry describes the expansion as a grand tale of high-seas adventure, full of new characters, items, and bosses. And in case that trailer isn't enough, here's a gallery of in-game screenshots for Sea of Sorrow: The Cherry Time livestream also showed off a trio of new games on the way, and they all look delightful. First up was Blokkan: Secret of the Walking City, a video game based on a comic book about a robot detective who investigates cases. It features hand-drawn art, and it plays like a love letter to the golden age of adventure games. Next up was Radio Rain, a 2D pixel-art side-scroller where you play as a young girl named Cass, trapped in a ruined, rainy world. Inspired by '80s music, Cass searches rain-spattered streets, fights mischievous creatures, and works alongside her spirit companion to find a way home. Finally, The Botanist and the Translator closed out the new reveals. As the plant detective Hatti, players will investigate a planet-spanning plant mystery alongside her trusty translator, Oliver, in this breezy, beautiful adventure.

title: Alan Wake Dev’s Forgotten TV-Action Game Hybrid Is At A Huge Discount Right Now
description: I loved Quantum Break. In fact, I dare say that I still love it to this day. Combining Remedy’s pizzazz for third-person shooters with the boldness to add TV show elements to the narrative experience, Quantum Break’s time-bending power fantasy is one that hooked me from start to finish. After playing it at launch, I let the dust settle before playing it once again in the early 2020s, and now, it’s time for another playthrough—and you may as well join me when it’s this cheap. After Alan Wake’s horror-led approach, with Stephen King vibes oozing from the entire experience, I don’t think any of us expected it to become a larger part of a connected universe. Quantum Break may not officially be part of the same universe, but it feels like the foundation of what would eventually become Remedy’s connected universe. You play as Jack Joyce, who, after catching up with his time-machine-making friend Paul Serene, is interrupted by Jack’s brother, Will, who says using it will cause time to end. Of course, if that happened, the game wouldn’t continue. Instead, both Jack and Paul are afflicted by chronon radiation, giving the pair time-related abilities. Soldiers appear, causing a ruckus on the university campus, led by an older, more dangerous Paul. Gasp! It’s no surprise that a narrative focusing on time-travel shenanigans offers, well, time-travel shenanigans. But between missions, you’ll get to see real actors playing the characters in a series-style format, which gives you a nice break between some incredibly fun missions. That’s right, Remedy’s continued prowess in third-person shooter action is still here, and the time abilities give you some truly fun ways to deal with enemies. You can send out bubbles that freeze enemies in place, fire a barrage of bullets into them, and watch them die a horrible death by countless simultaneous bullets. A dash lets you close the gap between Jack and any enemies giving you trouble from a distance, while a blast lets you levitate…

title: I Was Wrong About GTA 6
description: Some months ago, I wrote about how, even prior to its full reveal, we already knew what GTA 6 was going to be. Although not unique to the franchise by any means, GTA games had always followed a very clear formula, rarely upending it in any meaningful way. I strongly suspected that the 13-year wait for GTA 6 would result in a very pretty version of a very familiar game. As release approached, I worried that for all of the praise heaped upon its story and incredible level of detail, all of that was merely a veneer on the same game we've been playing for 25 years. And in many ways, that is true; at its most basic level, GTA 6 is still a game about driving from point A to point B, and maybe shooting some ne'er-do-wells when you get there. But I dramatically underestimated the impact of that veneer, and just how differently a familiar formula can feel when accompanied by impactful systems and relationships. The freeform nature of GTA 6's world, and the objectives you have over the course of a given mission, are largely identical to previous games. You can just drive around and make your own fun, or deal with violent drug smugglers, or pilot a boat or plane or car through a series of checkpoints. It's all very familiar on paper. But never before in a GTA game have I considered whether I have time to go and do one of those things because I have someone I care about waiting at home. Only rarely in a GTA have I decided to drive carefully, lest I face the consequences of doing almost anything I'd traditionally associate with a GTA game. So much of GTA 6's focus is on the relationship between Lucia and Jason. I quickly found myself caring about them both, and for all of Rockstar's talk of their romantic relationship being optional, I truly can't fathom playing this in a way that doesn't fully embrace their love. And the way that permeates things even in Chapter 1--the phone calls, the text messages, the interactions at home--has forced some degree of role-playing on me. I…

It was a game about a comet, hurtling through the unknown. It wasn't clear what you'd do in this game, whether you'd control the comet itself or the space it moved through. It wasn't clear if this was some kind of arcade game, or a new spin on the endless runner, or even just a kind of cosmic sandbox. All I had was the comet and a name: Faraway. Faraway! I was captivated. Read more

It's time to play stealth tactics sim Cyber Knights: Flashpoint the way it was meant to be played: skulking in a hole while buzzing, clanking mechabastards cleanse the map of any and all defenders. title: How To Get A Helicopter In GTA 6
description: You’ll spend so many hours driving across the state of Leonida in Grand Theft Auto 6, that your feet will start to ache in the real world. But there are still other modes of travel that you can try out. And, yes, you can take to the skies as well on board a helicopter. In This Article Helicopter spawns in Grand Theft Auto 6 Early-game option: Buckingham Maverick Military helicopters in GTA 6 Amphibious helicopters Rooftop helipads in Vice City Helicopter spawns in Grand Theft Auto 6 As of the time of this writing, there’s no clear way to permanently own a helicopter in GTA 6. These vehicles can neither be saved near your safehouse, nor can they be delivered to wherever you are. That said, there are several areas where helicopters frequently spawn. For the most part, you should look at helipad markings on the map--i.e. “H” symbol on rooftops and facilities. We’ve got a few examples below. Early-game option: Buckingham Maverick The Buckingham Maverick is a great early-game pick if you just want to explore and reveal more of the map. To find it, simply travel along the main highway from Jason’s home and keep going southwest until you reach Southwind. To the right, you’ll see MHH Marque Hoppers, which has a Maverick conveniently parked on the pier. Military helicopters in GTA 6 While you’re in the area, you might be interested in getting a military helicopter in GTA 6. There are several options like the machine-gunning Buzzard, sleek Valkyrie, and beefy Cargobob. All of these are in the Mile Zero Base just a short distance away from Southwind. You must be careful, though, because this is a military base that’s on high alert. If you get spotted within its boundaries, you’ll be warned by police and soldiers. Dawdle for too long and you’ll be reported for committing a crime, earning an instant 4-star Wanted Level for good measure. Having countless troops, including those in armored vehicles, shooting at you is not a good way to start the day. Amphibious helicopters It’s…

title: How To Steal And Register Cars With Advanced Trackers In GTA 6
description: Grand Theft Auto 6 has a massive world, and you can be sure that there are thousands of vehicles driving across the countryside at any given point in time. While the vast majority can be hijacked without worries--well, aside from cops that might see you--a select few have anti-theft devices that make them an unbearable hassle. Thankfully, there are ways to steal vehicles with Advanced Trackers. Advanced Trackers: How exactly do they work? The Advanced Trackers in GTA 6 can be seen if you scan most high-end vehicles like sports cars and luxury cars. Basically, if it looks expensive and sells for a high price, you can bet that it has an Advanced Tracker. Here’s how the device works: Stolen vehicles with a Standard Tracker ping their location only if (a) they’ve significantly slowed down or stopped, and (b) a police car is nearby. Advanced Trackers, meanwhile, ping their location if you go below a certain speed. You essentially need to put your pedal to the metal when driving them. Otherwise, the police would know your exact location. Given the risk, most fence NPCs in the game won’t even accept stolen vehicles with Advanced Trackers. Well, except for one fella: Randy. The legit method: Do missions for Randy Randy is the one NPC in the game that accepts stolen cars with Advanced Trackers, but there are some caveats: You meet Randy while tackling main missions in chapter 3. He’ll give you a task to steal a Zorrusso, which also nets you the Key Cloner, a tool that allows you to hijack keyless cars. At this point, Randy and various Pay ‘n’ Spray shops will start accepting stolen vehicles with Standard Trackers. He’ll also tell you that he has a “wishlist” of sorts: A dozen or so high-end cars that you need to boost and bring to his garage. Note that some targets do have Advanced Trackers. He’ll only accept these as long as they’re part of his wishlist. Since he’ll keep them, you won’t be able to own/register them at all. Again, you need to drive fast to prevent the…

title: All GTA 6 Book Swap Locations
description: Those who grew up in the 80s and 90s would remember things known as gamebooks, the precursors to modern-day role-playing and narrative-driven games. You might recall the Choose Your Own Adventure series and R.L. Stine’s Give Yourself Goosebumps, which presented you with choices, making you turn page after page to see the outcome. Further back, we had classics like the Sorcery series and The Warlock of Firetop Mountain--co-written by authors Steve Jackson and Ian Livingstone, who coincidentally also founded Games Workshop (yes, the very company that owns Warhammer). Grand Theft Auto 6 pays homage to these works in the form of book swap locations, which you can find all over Leonida. In This Article Book Swap collectibles in Grand Theft Auto 6 Book Swaps in Mariana County Book Swap #1 Book Swap #2 Book Swap #3 Book Swaps in Vice-Dale County Book Swap #4 Book Swap #5 Book Swaps in Leonard County and Kelly County Book Swap #6 Book Swap #7 Book Swap collectibles in Grand Theft Auto 6 The book swaps in GTA 6 can be found in public bookcases outside homes--i.e. akin to little free libraries. Once you spot one, interact with it to browse the book’s contents. Yes, they function similarly to magazines and comics in that you can read a few excerpts. However, they’re part of a separate tally in the Collections page. The literary works have silly dilemmas and humorous outcomes. It’s not quite interactive as, say, Tenebrae Lux on the JoyStation, but it’s still a nice nod that fans of gamebooks would appreciate. Book Swaps in Mariana County Book Swap #1 Pick Your Path: Horror - Killer Prom Location: Inside a turtle-shaped container in the northeastern end of Dolphin Drive. Book Swap #2 Pick Your Path: Fantasy - The Wizard’s Ruin Location: Found in Beaumont Avenue in Watson Bay. It’s inside a blue bookcase in front of a white house. title: GTA 6 Has Massive Underground Caves Worth Diving Into
description: Take a break from all the car chases and crimes in Grand Theft Auto 6, and relax in the quaint Emerald Springs resort. Oh, what's that? Is there something interesting nearby? Yes, it looks like a tourist attraction, the Selkie Hole, is worth a look. Perhaps there are hidden rewards that await you in the depths of the underwater cave. In This Article Where to find the Selkie Hole in Grand Theft Auto 6 The blue pools Cave diving for rewards and following the ropes More tunnels and meteorites Potential for more secrets: The Hollow Earth theory Where to find the Selkie Hole in Grand Theft Auto 6 The Selkie Hole in GTA 6 can be found in Kelly County. Specifically, it’s in a large nature reserve known as Emerald Springs. To get there, follow the road leading southeast out of Port Gellhorn or west from Hamlet. The blue pools Upon arriving, be sure to check the nearby scannables using your WAiNK app. Then, make your way to the western part of the park as shown on the map above. You’ll find a visually striking place, a pool with crystal clear blue water. From there, look for a small shed that has the Selkie Hole signage. This leads to the diving area, which also has Scuba Gear for you and your partner to equip. Likewise, note that the cave entrance here counts as a WAiNK Curiosity when scanned. Cave diving for rewards and following the ropes From the diving area, keep to the left as you go underwater. You’ll see a ropeline with arrows. The arrows actually point toward the exit which, in this case, is the diving area itself. So, for now, follow the rope as it leads in the opposite direction. Along the way, you’ll be able to pick up a couple of meteorites and the Explorer’s Knife legendary weapon. You’ll end up at the other end of the tunnel--i.e. the pool with clear blue water. Note: Pay attention to the remaining oxygen in your oxygen tank. You have to return to the diving area if you want to refill it or equip your Scuba Gear again. More tunnels and meteorites But that’s…

title: Xbox Game Pass Kicks Off December With Horror, Cozy Adventures, And More
description: One last month of 2026 brings two more waves of Xbox Game Pass titles to close out the year. Subscribers can once again look forward to some new arrivals in the Xbox Game Pass library, ranging from gruesome co-op action to wholesome adventures featuring helpful mice on a mission. These announcements typically come in two waves, with a sneak peek split between them, so while this list isn’t complete yet, we do know what you can expect in the first half of December. As usual, we’ll update this page once Xbox reveals the full lineup for this first batch. For now, you can look forward to an eclectic mix of games, starting with The Outlast Trials. Released in 2024, it’s a co-op survival-horror game that throws a team of up to four players into a gauntlet of deadly trials, where evasion is key to victory. You can also play it solo, and if the onslaught of festive season cheerfulness is getting to you, then this will be a nice–but brutal–change of pace. If you’d prefer to focus on the coziness of the season, then Hela: Of Mice and Magic looks like a fun time. Set in a magical forest inspired by Scandinavian lands, the game follows a group of mice on a journey to help people, at the behest of an old witch who can’t make the trip herself. This is also a day-one release for Xbox Game Pass, and it’ll be joined by World of Tanks Blitz on the same day. On December 3, Freestyle Football 2 launches, bringing fast-paced, 5v5 multiplayer street soccer to Xbox and PC, and on December 14, you can grab Nubby’s Number Factory, a roguelite game all about making big numbers. Xbox Game Pass December Wave 1 Games December 1 The Outlast Trials (Cloud, Xbox Series X|S, and PC) — Game Pass Ultimate, Game Pass Premium, PC Game Pass Hela: Of Mice and Magic (Cloud, Xbox Series X|S, and PC) — Game Pass Ultimate, PC Game Pass World of Tanks Blitz December 3 Freestyle Football 2 December 14 Nubby’s Number Factory If you missed it, November brought a solid selection of releases. title: All NoFlusher Tags In GTA 6
description: Grand Theft Auto 6 has several moments that rely heavily on over-the-top silliness. One, in particular, involves poo. Specifically, it’s about a group of individuals who do not want people to waste their, uh, waste, for fear of cloning and other sinister machinations. So, when you’re ready, it’s time to meet the gang and collect the NoFlusher Tags. The NoFlusher narrative arcs in Grand Theft Auto 6 If you’ve been gathering collectibles all over Leonida, you’ve likely chanced upon a strange WAiNK Curiosity, that of a NoFlushers Homestead. One pamphlet that’s been left behind even coerces citizens to avoid flushing their feces down the toilet. Instead, folks are encouraged to turn poop into odd by-products like pottery, soap, and even organic food. It’s downright disgusting, but it’s guaranteed to make you chuckle, too. Now, assuming you’ve made your way to Vice City, you’ll be given the opportunity to join the group proper: First, you need to use the WAiNK app on your phone to scan the “Stop! Don’t Flush! #NoFlushers” QR code. You can find this poster/QR code in public bathrooms, like the one in Dynamix Gym just north of your safehouse in chapter 3. Once you’ve done that, someone will tell you to meet up at Frank’s Waffles, and you’ll be able to mark the location on your map. This leads to a mission called The Final Flush. title: Dark fantasy and sudoku fuse together in unholy matrimony in Dungoku, a dungeon crawling twist on the classic puzzle game
description: Maths is not my strong suit, I make no secret of this, so when I come face to face with something like sudoku I will admit to recoiling in fear at having to confront this issue. Numbers don't make sense to me at the best of times, and now I have to figure out the specific placements of them whereby each number can only be used once per section, and each column and row have to all contain numbers one through nine? Terrifying! No, thanks, I'd much rather do the exact same thing but with, I don't know, skeletons and ghouls and the like. Which, conveniently, is more or less what Dungoku offers, a genre mashup of dungeon crawling and sudoku with a retro dark fantasy vibe. Read more
